message.content:
Below are two ways to create a **Google Cloud Compute Engine** instance that has an **NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU** and runs **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.

> ⚠️ **Note**  
> *Google Cloud does not use the “EC2” terminology – that’s Amazon Web Services. In GCP the service is called **Compute Engine**.*  
> *The RTX A6000 is available only in certain zones (e.g., `us-central1-a`, `us-east1-b`, `us-east1-c`, `us-east1-d`, `us-east1-f`). Make sure the zone you pick supports GPUs.*

---

## 1. Using the `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# Variables
PROJECT="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"          # pick a zone that supports RTX A6000
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --project="$PROJECT" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --machine-type="n1-standard-8" \   # 8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM (adjust as needed)
  --image-family="ubuntu-2004-lts" \
  --image-project="ubuntu-os-cloud" \
  --boot-disk-size="100GB" \
  --boot-disk-type="pd-ssd" \
  --accelerator="type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1" \
  --maintenance-policy="TERMINATE" \
  --restart-on-failure \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh   # optional: your init script
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM configuration. `n1-standard-8` gives 8 vCPUs & 30 GB RAM. |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Pull the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image. |
| `--boot-disk-size` & `--boot-disk-type` | SSD boot disk of 100 GB. |
| `--accelerator` | Adds one RTX A6000 GPU. |
| `--maintenance-policy` | `TERMINATE` means the VM will be stopped if the host is reclaimed. |
| `--restart-on-failure` | Auto‑restart if the VM crashes. |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script` | Optional shell script that runs on first boot. |

> **Tip**: If you need more GPUs, change `count=2` (or more) but remember that each GPU adds cost and may require a different machine type.

---

## 2. Using the REST API (JSON)

If you prefer to call the Compute Engine API directly (e.g., from a script or a CI/CD pipeline), use the following POST request.

```http
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances
Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_OAUTH_TOKEN>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        {
          "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT",
          "name": "External NAT"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorType": "projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000",
      "acceleratorCount": 1
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update\napt-get install -y build-essential"
      }
    ]
  },
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": [
        "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "tags": {
    "items": ["http-server", "https-server"]
  }
}
```

### Replace placeholders

| Placeholder | Example / Explanation |
|-------------|-----------------------|
| `{project}` | Your GCP project ID (e.g., `my-gcp-project`). |
| `{zone}` | Zone that supports GPUs (e.g., `us-central1-a`). |
| `<YOUR_OAUTH_TOKEN>` | OAuth 2.0 token with `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/compute` scope. |

### Authentication

You can obtain an OAuth token via:

```bash
gcloud auth application-default print-access-token
```

or by using a service account key:

```bash
export GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS="/path/to/key.json"
gcloud auth activate-service-account --key-file=$GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS
```

Then use the token in the `Authorization` header.

---

## Quick Checklist

1. **Zone** – Verify the zone supports RTX A6000 (`us-central1-a`, `us-east1-b`, etc.).
2. **Machine type** – Ensure it meets your CPU/RAM needs.
3. **GPU count** – Adjust `acceleratorCount` if you need more than one GPU.
4. **Billing** – GPUs incur additional charges; enable billing for the project.
5. **Firewall** – Add firewall rules if you need external access (the example adds `http-server` and `https-server` tags).

With either the `gcloud` command or the REST API call, you’ll have a Compute Engine instance running Ubuntu 20.04 LTS with an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU ready for your workloads. Happy computing!
